properties.name: MEASURED 2026-09-20: six tools still send the payload twice to every client, and the per-client shape is a no-op on all six — a second reply-builder in skills_tools.rs predates the signpost change and nothing enumerates the surface to notice
properties.statement: MEASURED 2026-09-20 against a real binary (target/debug/reflow2-mcp, one scratch graph per client, no --content-policy flag), three handshake names, eight tools each. Six tools return the payload duplicated into the text block, byte-identical across claude-code, opencode and grok-build: get_instructions (text 31,187 / structured 31,374 / wire 64,120), list_skills (21,123 / 20,119 / 42,568), get_skill (16,844 / 17,315 / 35,099), find_skills (1,350 / 1,130 / 2,716), usage_report (5,690 / 4,415 / 10,873), design_identity (111 / 101 / 317). The controls in the same processes varied correctly: loop_status and graph_report gave the signpost to claude-code, an empty block to opencode, a duplicate to grok-build. A session opening with get_instructions, list_skills and one get_skill pays 141,787 bytes on the wire for 68,808 of payload — the signpost shape would cost about 72,800, so 47% of it is the copy that fact:every-reply-was-sent-twice says was removed on 2026-08-23. Two consequences beyond the cost. The per-client policy is INERT on exactly these six: content_policy::apply returns early unless the reply is already in signpost shape, so opencode's Empty never fires and its measured empty-block fallback is defeated on the very tools that carry the instructions and the skills. And grok is served correctly only by accident. THE INSTANCE is a private helper, fn structured at crates/reflow2-mcp/src/tools/skills_tools.rs:554, whose doc comment asserts "Same shape every other tool returns: structured content plus readable text" — true when it was written, false since PR #304 made json_result a signpost, and read by nothing since. Its last touch was PR #262, a module-cycle refactor, so it predates the change that was supposed to end this and was never migrated. THE CLASS is that the reply-shape invariant is pinned by INSTANCE rather than by enumeration: tests/reply_is_sent_once.rs asserts the property on detect_gaps alone, and ver:a-reply-takes-the-shape-its-client-can-read checks one tool on the wire, in a crate that already carries a dozen checks which enumerate the served surface (every_constructor_can_say_what_the_thing_is, every_required_parameter_is_described, one_tool_declares_its_output_contract and more). A surface-enumerating check would have failed on the day #304 landed, because the helper already existed then; the instance fix stops today's six and leaves the next builder free to drift the same way. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether get_skill and get_instructions SHOULD duplicate, since they carry documents a content-only client must actually read — ok_markdown exists for exactly that and is a third answer. No Decision records a choice either way, and no test in the suite reads the text block of any of the six, so nothing depends on the current shape. That question belongs with dec:idea-how-does-a-content-only-client-get-an-answer and dec:idea-what-should-the-reply-shape-be-for-a-client-nobody-has-measured, and is the owner's to settle. ALSO NOT ESTABLISHED: latent.rs and degraded.rs duplicate at four more sites, which is defensible there (a client that cannot read the refusal learns nothing) and was not investigated.
